title: RTL-CJK punctuation + numeric normalization probe bank
content:
Purpose:
This working prompt-bank is designed for model onboarding regressions that focus on punctuation and numeric/date/time normalization across CJK (zh, ja, ko) and RTL (ar, he) locales. The aim is to surface subtle formatting regressions that harm downstream UX (parsing, display, search) even when semantic translation quality is acceptable.

Scope and motivation:
- Focus on normalization behaviors that commonly differ between locales: full-width vs half-width punctuation, ideographic comma (、) vs ASCII comma, Arabic-Indic digits vs Western digits, comma/period decimal separators, date order and separators, space insertion around punctuation, quotation mark variants, parentheses/brackets, ellipses.
- Evaluate both direct normalization ("normalize this string for X locale") and translation outputs for preservation/correction of local formatting when translating user-provided snippets.
- Include edge cases that trigger KV-cache or tokenizer quirks (adjacent punctuation to CJK characters, bidi contexts mixing LTR/RTL and neutral punctuation).

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Input set: ~320 prompts (80 per subcategory) split across languages and subtopics; run deterministically with seeds, and with streaming/long-context variants.
- Metrics: normalization-accuracy (%) = exact match of normalized target; token-normalization-f1 (tolerant of whitespace differences); locale-formatting-score (heuristic scoring for dates/numeric outputs); human spot-check for translation-induced mis-normalization (5% sample).
- Regression thresholds: fail if normalization-accuracy drops by >=5 percentage points vs baseline for any subcategory, or if locale-formatting-score drops below 90 for critical flows (dates, currency).
- Run cadence: pre-release smoke for model candidate, full regression for major/:minor bumps.

Prompt bank structure (examples, not exhaustive):
1) Punctuation width and spacing (CJK)
- Prompt: "Normalize the following text for display in zh-Hans: '买了3，件衣服。。。价格：12.50USD (含运费)，谢谢！'"
- Expected normalized: "买了3件衣服……价格：12.50 美元（含运费），谢谢！"

- Prompt: "Normalize: '今日は、いい天気 です 。' for ja-JP."
- Expected normalized: "今日はいい天気です。"

2) Ideographic vs ASCII comma and punctuation placement
- Prompt: "Normalize Korean: '오늘은,날씨가좋다,정말'"
- Expected: "오늘은, 날씨가 좋다, 정말" (note: insert space after commas per ko conventions)

3) Quotation marks and nested quotes (CJK)
- Prompt: "Convert to zh-Hant typographically correct quotes: 'She said: \"I\'ll come at 5:00.\"'"
- Expected: "她說：「我會在5:00到。」"

4) Arabic-Indic digits and decimal separators (RTL)
- Prompt: "Normalize for ar-EG: 'السعر 12.5 USD, تم شراء 3 items.'"
- Expected: "السعر ١٢٫٥٠ دولارًا، تم شراء ٣ عناصر."

5) Bidirectional punctuation mixing and neutral characters (RTL + LTR tokens)
- Prompt: "User text: 'الملف report_v2(최종).pdf جاهز' — normalize for ar-SA."
- Expected: "الملف report_v2(최종).pdf جاهز" (ensure parentheses attach to Korean token properly; preserve ASCII filename but maintain correct surround punctuation order for bidi semantics)

6) Dates and locale order (CJK vs RTL)
- Prompt: "Normalize to ja-JP date format: '03/04/2026' (source ambiguous). Assume user is Japanese."
- Expected: "2026年03月04日"

- Prompt: "Normalize to ar-SA short date: '04-03-2026' (day-month-year)"
- Expected: "٠٤‏/٠٣‏/٢٠٢٦" (Arabic-Indic digits and RTL separators)

7) Numeric grouping separators and currency placement
- Prompt: "Normalize for zh-TW: 'total: 1,234,567.89 USD'"
- Expected: "總計：1,234,567.89 美元" (preserve grouping but local order and currency label)

8) Ellipses, repeated punctuation, and truncation markers
- Prompt: "Normalize for ko-KR: '그는... 갔다!!! 왜??'"
- Expected: "그는…… 갔다!!! 왜??" (normalize three dots to ideographic ellipsis when adjacent to CJK, but preserve emphatic exclamation/question sequences)

9) Translation + normalization edgecases (preserve numeric literals)
- Prompt: "Translate to ar and normalize: 'Call me at +1 (415) 555-0132 at 5:30pm.'"
- Expected: "اتصل بي على +1 (415) 555-0132 في الساعة ٥:٣٠ م." (translate words, keep international number, convert time digits to Arabic-Indic)

10) Ambiguous punctuation in mixed-script chat snippets
- Prompt: "User wrote: 'Hey، كيف الحال؟ I'm fine، thanks.' Normalize to ar-EG."
- Expected: "Hey، كيف الحال؟ I'm fine، thanks." (do not erroneously translate/normalize English fragments; keep punctuation appropriate for surrounding script)

Test harness notes and generation settings:
- Run with tokenization that mirrors production SDK (same vocab). Document any post-processing we expect from the client (e.g., normalization layer in Redwood Console) so we test model output + postproc together.
- For translation tasks include 2 modes: 1) "translate preserving numeric/formatting tokens" and 2) "translate and localize formatting". Record which mode each prompt targets.

Labeling and gold creation:
- Golds created by native speakers and localization engineers. For ambiguous cases include 2 acceptable variants and mark one as preferred. Use 'tolerant-match' labels for whitespace-only differences.

Known risk cases to monitor (examples observed in earlier onboarding runs):
- Model strips full-width punctuation in CJK contexts when compression/quantization applied (seen in vX.12 candidate).
- RTL numeral conversion sometimes fails for embedded LTR tokens (time stamps inside ASCII parentheses).
- Bidi reordering issues where neutral punctuation migrates to wrong side after translation -> breaks parsers that rely on fixed byte offsets.

Actionable TODOs:
- [ ] Expand numeric/date subbank to include monthly/quarterly fiscal formats and timezone-aware timestamps (Samir).
- [ ] Add 40 additional Arabic/Hebrew prompts that include Hebrew points (niqqud) and Arabic tashkeel edgecases (Lena).
- [ ] Hook the prompt bank into the nightly regression DAG and surface per-subcategory deltas in the Roche dashboard (Diego).
- [ ] Add a small automated human-review sampling job that picks false positives for normalization-accuracy (Priya).

Open questions for reviewers:
- For ja/zh/ko should we prefer full-width numerals within purely CJK text? Current preference: preserve ASCII numerals except when requested to localize. Does that match product expectations?
- How much tolerance for whitespace insertion after commas in ko? Some UI teams prefer no added spaces for compact displays.

Appendix: quick run commands (local harness)
- python tools/run_eval.py --prompt-bank=rtl-cjk-punct-normalization-probe-bank-2026.json --model=candidate --mode=normalize,translate --out=results/candidate-2026-03-04.json

History / notes:
- Created as a focused companion to the broader locale-guided-translation-probe-suite. This file intentionally drills into punctuation/normalization failure modes that frequently cause downstream parsing bugs reported by Solutions Engineering.

If you add prompts, please follow the filename and short prompt guideline at the top of the company prompt style doc and include one-line justification for inclusion.
